zh: 四、明愚癡發相，自有三種：一、計斷常；二、計有無；三、計世性。此三並是著眾邪見，不出生死，是故通名愚癡。一、計斷常癡者，行者於修定中，忽爾發邪思惟，利心分別：「過去我及諸法為滅，而有現在我及諸法邪？為不滅而有邪？」因是思惟，見心即發，推尋三世，若謂滅，即墮斷中；若謂不滅，即墮常中。如是癡覺，念念不住，因此利智捷疾，辯才無滯，諍競戲論，作諸惡行，能障正定出世之法，是為計斷常癡發之相。
en: Fourth, clarifying that delusion has three differing marks of arising: holding to annihilationism or eternalism; holding to existence or nonexistence; and holding to a fixed worldly nature. All three of these are attachment to various wrong views, none of them leading out of birth-and-death — hence they are called, in general, delusion.

First, the delusion of holding to annihilationism or eternalism: the practitioner, within cultivating concentration, suddenly gives rise to a deviant train of thought, discriminating with a sharp mind: "Have the self and every other dharma of the past ceased, so that the self and every dharma of the present now exist? Or have they not ceased, and so continue to exist?" Reflecting in this way, the mind of view at once arises, tracing back through the three periods of time — if it is held that they have ceased, one falls into annihilationism; if it is held that they have not ceased, one falls into eternalism. Such a deluded discursive mind, never remaining still moment to moment, brings with it a sharp and quick intelligence, an eloquence with nothing to obstruct it, given over to disputation and idle discourse, and every manner of unwholesome conduct — able to obstruct right concentration and the world-transcending Dharma. This is the mark of the delusion of holding to annihilationism or eternalism arising.

zh: 二、計有無癡發者，亦於修定之時，忽爾分別，思惟覺觀，謂今我及陰等諸法為定有耶？為定無耶？乃至非有非無耶？如是推尋，見心即發，隨見生執，以為定實邪覺，念念不住，因此利智捷疾，戲論諍競，起諸邪行，障礙於正定，不得開發，是為計有無癡發之相。
en: Second, the arising of the delusion of holding to existence or nonexistence: likewise, at the time of cultivating concentration, one suddenly discriminates, reflecting with discursive thought on whether the present self and the aggregates and other such dharmas definitely exist, or definitely do not exist, or, further still, neither exist nor do not exist. Tracing this back in this way, the mind of view at once arises, and, following whatever view arises, one clings to it as definitely real — a deviant discursive mind never remaining still moment to moment, bringing with it a sharp and quick intelligence, idle discourse and disputation, giving rise to every kind of deviant conduct, obstructing right concentration so that it cannot be brought forth. This is the mark of the delusion of holding to existence or nonexistence arising.

zh: 三、計世性癡發者，亦於修定之時，忽作是念：「由有微塵，所以即有實法；有實法故，便有四大；有四大故，而有假名眾生及諸世界。」如是思惟，見心即發，念念不住，因此利智辯才，能問能說，高心自舉，是非諍競，專行邪行，離真實道，乃至思惟分別剎那之心亦復如是。以是因緣，不得發諸禪定，設發禪定，墮邪定聚，是為計世性癡發之相。
en: Third, the arising of the delusion of holding to a fixed worldly nature: likewise, at the time of cultivating concentration, one suddenly has this thought: "Because there are subtle particles, there is therefore a real dharma; because there is a real dharma, there are therefore the four elements; because there are the four elements, there are therefore sentient beings and the various worlds, existing only as provisional names." Reflecting in this way, the mind of view at once arises, never remaining still moment to moment, bringing with it a sharp intelligence and eloquence, able to question and able to expound, exalting oneself with a haughty mind, given over to disputes over right and wrong, devoted single-mindedly to deviant conduct, straying far from the true path — and even the thought that discriminates a single instant of mind is exactly the same. Because of this, dhyāna-concentration cannot be brought forth at all; and even should dhyāna-concentration be brought forth, one falls into the group of those fixed in wrongness. This is the mark of the delusion of holding to a fixed worldly nature arising.

All three marks of delusion share the same telltale symptom: a sharp and quick intelligence (with unobstructed eloquence named explicitly for the first and third), not dullness — delusion here is explicitly an intellectual's affliction, wrong views seized on and defended with real cleverness rather than simple confusion. Holding to existence or nonexistence directly inverts the tetralemma-style analyses fascicle 3 used against "contaminated dharma" and "karma cannot be found" — there, the same four alternatives (existence, nonexistence, both, neither) were tested and found empty; here, seizing on any one of those same four alternatives as definitely true is itself classed as an unwholesome root.

items.zh: 明惡根性發 · 惡業障道

zh: 五、明惡業障道發相，亦有三種：一、沈昏闇蔽障；二、惡念思惟障；三、境界逼迫障。一、沈昏闇蔽障者，行者於修定欲用心之時，即便沈昏闇睡，無記瞪矒，無所別知，障諸禪定，不得開發，是為沈昏闇蔽障發之相。二、惡念思惟障者，若行者欲修定時，雖不沈昏闇睡，而惡念心生，或念欲作十惡、四重、五逆、毀禁、還俗等事，無時暫停，因是障諸禪定，不得開發，是為惡念思惟障發之相。
en: Fifth, clarifying that unwholesome karma obstructing the path has three differing marks of arising: the obstruction of sunken, dark dullness; the obstruction of unwholesome, deliberate thought; and the obstruction of oppressive states.

First, the obstruction of sunken, dark dullness: if the practitioner, at the very moment of wishing to apply the mind in cultivating concentration, immediately sinks into dark, dull drowsiness, blank and glazed over, aware of nothing distinctly, obstructing dhyāna-concentration so that it cannot be brought forth — this is the mark of the obstruction of sunken, dark dullness arising.

Second, the obstruction of unwholesome, deliberate thought: if the practitioner, wishing to cultivate concentration, though not sunk into dark, dull drowsiness, has an unwholesome thought arise instead — thinking, perhaps, of committing the ten unwholesome actions, the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, violating the precepts, returning to lay life, and other such matters, never pausing for a moment — thereby obstructing dhyāna-concentration so that it cannot be brought forth — this is the mark of the obstruction of unwholesome, deliberate thought arising.

zh: 三、境界逼迫障者，若行人於修定之時，雖無上事，而身或時卒痛，覺有逼迫之事，見諸外境，或見無頭手足、無眼目等，或見衣裳破壞，或復陷入於地，或復火來燒身，或見高崖而復墮落，二山隔障，羅剎虎狼，或復夢見有諸惡相，如是事皆是障道罪起，逼迫行人，或令驚怖，或時苦惱，如此種種，非可備說，是名境界逼迫障發之相。
en: Third, the obstruction of oppressive states: if the practitioner, at the time of cultivating concentration, though none of the matters above is present, suddenly feels pain somewhere in the body, sensing something oppressive taking place, and sees various external states — perhaps seeing bodies without head, hands, or feet, without eyes; or seeing clothing torn and ruined; or sinking into the earth; or fire coming to burn the body; or seeing a high cliff and then falling from it; or two mountains closing in to block the way; rākṣasas, tigers, and wolves; or, in dreams, seeing various unwholesome signs — all such matters as these arise from the offense that obstructs the path, oppressing the practitioner, at times causing terror, at times causing distress; such things are manifold and cannot be described in full. This is the mark of the obstruction of oppressive states arising.

zh: 今約此五不善法，即合為三障。前三毒，即為習因煩惱障。等分之中覺觀亂法，即是麁四陰，故名為報障。三種障道，即為業障。何以知之？由過去造惡，未來應受惡報，即以業持此惡。若行者於未受報中間而修善者，善與惡乖，業即扶惡而起，來障於善，故知即是業障。如是三障，障一切行人禪定、智慧不得開發，故名為障。
en: Here, with reference to these five unwholesome dharmas, they are brought together as three obstructions. The first three — the three poisons — form the obstruction of affliction, belonging to the habituation-cause. Within the equal-portion affliction, the disordered dharma of discursive thought is itself the coarse four aggregates, and so is called the obstruction of retribution. The three kinds of the path's obstruction described above form the obstruction of karma. How is this known? Because of unwholesome deeds committed in the past, unwholesome retribution is bound to be received in the future, and it is karma itself that sustains this unwholesomeness. If the practitioner, in the interval before that retribution is received, cultivates what is wholesome, the wholesome and the unwholesome come into conflict, and the karma rises up in support of the unwholesome, coming to obstruct the wholesome — hence it is known that this is precisely the obstruction of karma. These three obstructions obstruct every practitioner's dhyāna-concentration and wisdom from being brought forth at all — hence they are called obstructions.

This closing regrouping — five unwholesome dharmas collapsing into the three classical obstructions of the Buddhist tradition (affliction, retribution, and karma) — gives the fifteen marks just described their place within a much older framework than this treatise's own five-gate scheme. The three obstructions also explain something the marks themselves only show from the inside: why a practitioner sincerely trying to do good can feel actively opposed by their own unwholesome karma rising up "in support of the unwholesome" — not a failure of effort, but a named mechanism the treatise says the antidotes that follow are meant to address directly. This closes the second of verifying unwholesome capacity's four parts.

zh: 第三、次明對治法者，對名主對，治名為治，如不淨觀主治婬欲，故名對治。如是乃至念佛三昧等，主治惡業障道。今明對治中，自有六意不同：一者、對治治；二者、轉治；三者、不轉治；四者、兼治；五者、兼轉兼不轉治；六者、非對非轉非兼治。一、明對治者，前善惡根性發中，名為十五，今此對治中，亦為十五。問曰：此豈非煩長邪？答曰：不然。前為驗知故說，今為對治故說。前為約善根自發故說，今為修習故說，此非煩重。
en: Third, next clarifying the antidote methods: "matching" means governing the match, and "antidote" means to treat — as the contemplation of impurity is matched to govern lustful craving, hence it is called the matched antidote; in the same way, all the way through the buddha-recollection samādhi, which governs unwholesome karma obstructing the path. Here, within clarifying the antidotes, there are six differing senses: matched antidote treatment; transposed treatment; non-transposed treatment; combined treatment; combined transposed-and-non-transposed treatment; and treatment that is neither matched, transposed, nor combined.

First, clarifying the matched antidote: the fifteen marks named above, within the arising of wholesome and unwholesome capacity, are here given, in this discussion of antidotes, as fifteen once again. Question: is this not needlessly repetitive? Answer: this does not follow. What was said above was said for the sake of verification; what is said here is said for the sake of the antidote. What was said above was said with reference to a wholesome root's own arising; what is said here is said for the sake of cultivation — this is not mere repetition.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of delusion, and why are they all called delusion?
options: annihilationism or eternalism, existence or nonexistence, a fixed worldly nature — all attachment to wrong views, not leading out of birth-and-death
quiz.why: "Delusion has three differing marks of arising: holding to annihilationism or eternalism; holding to existence or nonexistence; and holding to a fixed worldly nature. All three of these are attachment to various wrong views, none of them leading out of birth-and-death — hence they are called, in general, delusion."

quiz.q: How does the delusion of annihilationism or eternalism arise?
options: tracing the three times, asking whether past self and dharmas ceased or not; holding they ceased is annihilationism, not ceased is eternalism
quiz.why: "'Have the self and every other dharma of the past ceased, so that the self and every dharma of the present now exist? Or have they not ceased, and so continue to exist?' ... if it is held that they have ceased, one falls into annihilationism; if it is held that they have not ceased, one falls into eternalism."

quiz.q: What does the text say typically accompanies the arising of these deluded views?
options: sharp, quick intelligence, unobstructed eloquence, disputation and idle discourse, unwholesome conduct, obstructing right concentration
quiz.why: "Such a deluded discursive mind, never remaining still moment to moment, brings with it a sharp and quick intelligence, an eloquence with nothing to obstruct it, given over to disputation and idle discourse, and every manner of unwholesome conduct — able to obstruct right concentration and the world-transcending Dharma."

quiz.q: What line of thought marks the delusion of a fixed worldly nature?
options: the self definitely exists or not
because there are particles there is real dharma; from it the four elements; from them provisionally named beings and worlds
quiz.why: "One suddenly has this thought: 'Because there are subtle particles, there is therefore a real dharma; because there is a real dharma, there are therefore the four elements; because there are the four elements, there are therefore sentient beings and the various worlds, existing only as provisional names.'"

quiz.q: If one holding a fixed worldly nature does attain some concentration, what happens?
options: it falls among the deviant concentrations
quiz.why: "Because of this, dhyāna-concentration cannot be brought forth at all; and even should some concentration be brought forth, it falls among the deviant concentrations."

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of unwholesome karma obstructing the path?
options: sunken dark dullness, unwholesome deliberate thought, oppressive states
quiz.why: "Unwholesome karma obstructing the path has three differing marks of arising: the obstruction of sunken, dark dullness; the obstruction of unwholesome, deliberate thought; and the obstruction of oppressive states." Affliction, karma, and retribution are the three obstructions into which all five are later combined.

quiz.q: In the obstruction of unwholesome deliberate thought, what does the practitioner think of?
options: committing the ten evils, the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, breaking precepts, returning to lay life, without pause
quiz.why: "Though not sunk into dark, dull drowsiness, has an unwholesome thought arise instead — thinking, perhaps, of committing the ten unwholesome actions, the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, violating the precepts, returning to lay life, and other such matters, never pausing for a moment."

quiz.q: In the obstruction of oppressive states, what may one see?
options: bodies without head or limbs, torn clothing, sinking into earth, fire, falling from cliffs, mountains closing in, rākṣasas and tigers
quiz.why: "Perhaps seeing bodies without head, hands, or feet, without eyes; or seeing one's own clothing torn and ruined; or sinking into the earth; or fire coming to burn the body; or standing on a high cliff and then falling from it; or two mountains closing in to block the way; rākṣasas, tigers, and wolves."

quiz.q: The five unwholesome dharmas combine into three obstructions. Which pairing is correct?
options: poisons = karma; thought = affliction; path = retribution
the three poisons = affliction; discursive disorder (the coarse four aggregates) = retribution; the three path obstructions = karma
quiz.why: "The first three — the three poisons — form the obstruction of affliction, belonging to the habituation-cause. Within the equal-portion affliction, the disordered dharma of discursive thought is itself the coarse four aggregates, and so is called the obstruction of retribution. The three kinds of the path's obstruction described above form the obstruction of karma."

quiz.q: Why, according to the text, does the obstruction of karma rise up when one cultivates the good?
options: past evil awaits retribution, sustained by karma; cultivating good in the interval, good and evil conflict, and karma rises in support of evil to obstruct the good
because the Buddha does not protect
quiz.why: "Because of unwholesome deeds committed in the past, unwholesome retribution is bound to be received in the future, and it is karma itself that sustains this unwholesomeness. If the practitioner, in the interval before that retribution is received, cultivates what is wholesome, the wholesome and the unwholesome come into conflict, and the karma rises up in support of the unwholesome."

quiz.q: The antidotes have six senses. Which list is correct?
options: matched, transposed, non-transposed, combined, combined transposed-and-not, neither matched nor transposed nor combined
quiz.why: "Within clarifying the antidotes, there are six differing senses: matched antidote treatment; transposed treatment; non-transposed treatment; combined treatment; combined transposed-and-non-transposed treatment; and treatment that is neither matched, transposed, nor combined."

quiz.q: Fifteen were already named in the arising of capacity; why is naming fifteen again for the antidotes not repetitive?
options: before it was for verification and spontaneous arising; now for the antidote and for cultivation
quiz.why: "What was said above was said for the sake of verification; what is said here is said for the sake of the antidote. What was said above was said with reference to a wholesome root's own arising; what is said here is said for the sake of cultivation — this is not mere repetition."
